method: Composes one systemd .socket unit from a base name, a description and one to eight ListenStream addresses. Addresses follow systemd.socket(5): a leading slash is an AF_UNIX file-system socket, a leading @ an AF_UNIX abstract socket, a single number a port listened on over IPv6 (dual-stack by default through BindIPv6Only=default), v.w.x.y:port an IPv4 socket, and [x]:y an IPv6 socket. File-system paths must be absolute, at most 4096 characters, free of backslashes, //, . and .. segments and a trailing slash, and fit in 107 bytes because sockaddr_un.sun_path is 108 with the terminator; abstract names need at least one character after @ and no whitespace. Ports are 1-65535 with no leading zeros; IPv4 hosts must be strict dotted quads and IPv6 hosts must be bracketed and valid, compared against a full compression-aware parser. Interface scopes (address%iface) and AF_VSOCK addresses are rejected rather than half-supported, because a literal percent would have to be doubled for unit-file specifier expansion. Addresses are emitted in input order, duplicates are refused, and spaces, double quotes and percent signs in unix names are written as \x20, \x22 and %% so the parser reads back the exact name. Accept=yes is emitted only when selected; it changes the companion unit to the template <base>@.service, where systemd starts one instance per connection and attaches the connection to the instance's standard input and output. With Accept=no the service receives every listening socket as file descriptors starting at 3 (sd_listen_fds(3)) and must not bind the address itself. MaxConnections is validated and written only with Accept=yes, and only when it differs from the default 64. SocketMode (four-digit octal), SocketUser and SocketGroup apply only to file-system unix sockets - the man page scopes the mode to file nodes - so they are ignored, not emitted, for TCP, IPv6, port-only and abstract addresses; SocketMode is written only when it differs from the default 0666, and parent directories are created with the default DirectoryMode=0755. The [Install] section with WantedBy=sockets.target is optional. The page reports the generated file name, the matching service name, the listen mix and the activation contract, warns that a bare port is an IPv6 wildcard and that a unix socket is not removed on stop, and never inspects the host or executes anything.
